description: Canonical TSV schema + entity-resolution layer — turns heterogeneous RawRecords from any adapter into coherent, deduplicated, Neo4j-import-compatible node and edge TSV files keyed on a stable global id reconciled to Wikidata QIDs and Getty ids, with typed headers, provenance, and round-trip-safe canonical ordering.

tasks.title: T2-US-001: Implement the canonical TSV header model
tasks.description:
As a developer, I need typed node/edge headers matching docs/data-model.md so files are Neo4j-import compatible.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Define NodeSchema and EdgeSchema describing required headers (csid:ID, :LABEL, name, ...) and typed property suffixes (:int, :float)
- Provide a function to render and parse a header row for nodes and for edges
- Reject property columns whose declared type suffix does not match the data model
- Tests pass (pytest) round-tripping a header row to schema objects and back
- Type checks pass (mypy)

Project context: culture-scrape — see PLAN.md, docs/data-model.md, docs/prior-art.md. Work in the repo root (src/culturescrape/). This story belongs to tasklist 'ralph/schema-entity-resolution'.

tasks.title: T2-US-002: Implement a strict TSV writer and reader
tasks.description:
As a developer, I need tab-delimited IO that never corrupts data containing tabs/newlines so files are lossless.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Writer escapes/encodes tab, newline, and backslash in field values deterministically; reader reverses it exactly
- Multi-value fields use ';' with a defined escape for literal ';'
- Header is always the first line; column order is stable
- Tests pass (pytest) writing then reading values containing tabs, newlines, and ';' and asserting equality
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T2-US-003: Implement csid minting
tasks.description:
As a developer, I need deterministic global ids so re-runs are idempotent.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- If a Wikidata QID is known, csid is derived deterministically from it (e.g. cs:<type>:Q<number>)
- Otherwise csid is cs:<type>:<deterministic slug/hash of normalized name+lang>
- Minting the same input twice yields the identical csid
- Tests pass (pytest) covering QID-based and name-based minting determinism
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T2-US-004: Implement field normalization
tasks.description:
As a developer, I want raw fields cleaned into canonical columns so downstream matching is reliable.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Normalize whitespace, unicode (NFC), and trim; map common source field names to canonical column names via a configurable mapping
- Parse temporal values into time_start:int / time_end:int (BCE negative) and keep raw in time_start_iso when ambiguous
- Parse coordinates into lat:float / lon:float; invalid coords are dropped with a logged warning
- Tests pass (pytest) for date parsing (BCE, century, year ranges) and coordinate parsing
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T2-US-006: Implement Wikidata QID reconciliation
tasks.description:
As a developer, I want entities matched to Wikidata so the same thing from two sources gets one id.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- When a row lacks a QID, attempt reconciliation via the Wikidata search/reconciliation API (cached client) using name+type+lang
- Accept a match only above a configurable score threshold; otherwise leave QID null and lower confidence
- Record the reconciliation decision (matched/none/ambiguous) in provenance
- Tests pass (pytest) against a recorded reconciliation API fixture covering match, no-match, and ambiguous cases
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T2-US-007: Implement Getty id reconciliation against local dumps
tasks.description:
As a developer, I want entities anchored to AAT/TGN/ULAN where applicable so vocabularies normalize types/places/people.

- Attach getty_id to a node when a confident label+type match exists
- No false anchor: ambiguous matches are skipped and logged

tasks.title: T2-US-008: Implement deduplication / entity resolution
tasks.description:
As a developer, I want duplicate entities collapsed so the graph has one node per real-world thing.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Resolution precedence: identical wikidata_qid > identical getty_id > exact normalized (name,lang,type) > fuzzy name match above threshold
- Merging unions aliases, keeps the highest-confidence value per column, and concatenates provenance from all merged rows
- Merge decisions are recorded so they can be audited and reversed
- Tests pass (pytest) merging a fixture with QID-dupes, label-dupes, and a fuzzy near-duplicate
- Type checks pass (mypy)
